title: Normalization Layers Are All That Sharpness-Aware Minimization Needs
main_claims: Perturbing only the affine normalization parameters (BatchNorm/LayerNorm, ~0.1% of parameters) in SAM's adversarial step outperforms perturbing all parameters across multiple SAM variants and architectures.
Alternative sparse perturbation methods do not achieve similar performance at the same extreme sparsity levels, demonstrating that this behavior is unique to normalization layers.

SAM-ON achieves higher generalization performance than SAM-all while finding sharper minima (higher measured sharpness), casting doubt on sharpness reduction as the sole explanation for SAM's effectiveness.
methodology: SAM-ON (SAM-OnlyNorm) is evaluated on WideResNet-28-10, ResNet-56, ResNeXt, and ViT-S/T architectures on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet, with SAM, ASAM, and Fisher-SAM variants. Sharpness is measured using logit-normalized worst-case adaptive ℓ∞ m-sharpness with 20-step AutoPGD in weight space (following Jiang et al.). Feature rank is measured following Andriushchenko et al. Computational wall-clock time comparisons are reported. SAM-ON is also evaluated for adversarial robustness and OOD performance on ImageNet variants (ImageNetV2, ImageNetR, ImageNetA, ImageNetSketch, ObjectNet).
key_results: SAM-ON achieves 84.19% on WRN-28-10/CIFAR-100 vs. 83.11% for SAM-all, while being sharper (20-step ℓ∞ sharpness 0.090 vs. 0.048 at ρ=0.003).
SAM-ON outperforms SAM-all on ImageNet OOD benchmarks (ImageNetR: 32.98% vs. 31.56%; ImageNetSketch: 19.35% vs. 18.50%; ObjectNet: 13.55% vs. 13.75%) for AdamW base optimizer on ViT-S/32.
Random mask at the same 99.93% sparsity as SAM-ON achieves only 80.97% vs. 84.19% for SAM-ON, confirming normalization layers specifically (not sparsity) drive the benefit.
limitations: The mechanism by which perturbing only normalization layers improves generalization while increasing sharpness remains unexplained; the paper identifies the phenomenon without fully explaining it.
SAM-ON does not always reduce wall-clock time compared to SAM-all because full backpropagation is still needed for gradient computation.
OOD evaluation is limited to ImageNet variants; no corruption benchmarks (CIFAR-C) are evaluated.
relevance_to_rq: Highly relevant to the RQ's core question: provides direct empirical evidence that SAM's generalization improvements are not solely caused by reduced sharpness (SAM-ON generalizes better but is sharper), supporting the hypothesis that other mechanisms—possibly representation-level effects—are at work. The OOD results on ImageNet variants are directly relevant to the ood_benchmarks sub-topic.

key_quotes.text: Although our findings reaffirm the effectiveness of SAM in improving generalization performance, they cast doubt on whether this is solely caused by reduced sharpness
key_quotes.context: Central claim of the paper challenging the sharpness-reduction explanation of SAM

key_quotes.text: the SAM-ON models obtain the best generalization performance, while having significantly higher sharpness than their SAM-all counterparts
key_quotes.context: Key empirical finding: better generalization without lower sharpness in SAM-ON

key_quotes.text: sparsity is not the sole cause for SAM-ON's success
key_quotes.context: Ruling out sparsity as explanation, isolating normalization layer perturbation as the operative factor
